verdict_label: Flexible socially, less so at work
explanation: Brazil is often described as running on 'hora brasileira' (Brazilian time) — for a social gathering or a visit to someone's home, arriving 15-30 minutes after the stated time is normal and not considered rude, and arriving exactly on time can even seem premature. Business meetings are different: Brazilians typically schedule in advance and increasingly expect punctuality, especially with senior executives, international partners, or in more formal industries.
local_tip: For business, aim to arrive on time or within a few minutes; for a purely social invitation to a home, treat the stated time as a loose guideline rather than a deadline.

also_check.note: Punctuality is strictly observed; even a few minutes late is considered disrespectful.
Being late is seen as unprofessional and reflects poorly on planning.
Arriving somewhat late to social gatherings is common and generally not seen as rude.
